_comment: Copy to src/aliases.json and fill in for your firm. The real file is gitignored — it names clients.
_aliases_comment: Maps the name a timesheet line uses to the name Legal One files it under. Drift runs both ways: a person may be registered under their company, and a company under the individual who is the client of record — the third example above points person-ward, the reverse of the first. Billing-relevant: a wrong entry books hours against the wrong entity and nothing surfaces the error, so this is reviewed like code rather than inferred at runtime.

internal._comment: Descriptions starting with any of these are firm-internal work, booked to the firm contact rather than a client matter.

defaults._comment: Firm constants — never asked in the interview, because they are the same on every matter this practice files. Every value below is tenant-specific and MUST be replaced: find your own ids with client.lookup(...), see the Lookups section of the README. A <placeholder> left in place makes Legal One reject the form with a 405. Origem and responsável are separate on purpose: a firm can file a matter under a practice-area node while the responsible office is the root, and one value for both writes the wrong one.

_titleFormat_comment: How this firm names a matter. Placeholders: {seq2} last two digits of the CNJ sequential, {check} its check digits, {year} {tribunal} {unit} the rest, {shortName} {description} as given, and {SHORTNAME} {DESCRIPTION} uppercased. Set it to null if the firm has no fixed convention — then no title is suggested, which is better than suggesting someone else’s.
